## Two-stream closures: the Meador-Weaver coefficients (Toon solver, `flags: planck`) {#sec-ch02-closures}

### Summary

A two-stream method keeps only the upward and downward fluxes of a layer and drops the angular detail of the
intensity. The equations for the two fluxes are exact moments of the transfer equation, but they contain two angular
integrals that the fluxes alone do not determine. A *closure* fixes them with an assumed angular shape of the
intensity. Every closure then gives the same pair of linear equations with four coefficients $\gamma_1$ to
$\gamma_4$ [@reading07]. pyharp's Toon solver uses the quadrature closure for the shortwave path and the hemispheric
mean for the longwave path [@reading02].

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The coefficients of @eq-ch02-closures-ode for each closure.

**Data.** Per layer: $\omega$, $g$ [-] and, for the beam, $\mu_0$ [-]; out: $\gamma_1$ to $\gamma_4$ [-].

**Placement.** Inside the layer loop of the Toon kernels, after delta scaling (@sec-ch02-delta-scaling).

**Activation.** `solver: toon`; `flags: planck` selects the longwave path; default shortwave.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact algebra; the two-stream error itself is not bounded here.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\omega$, single-scattering albedo [-]; $g$, asymmetry parameter [-];
$\mu_0$, cosine of the beam zenith angle [-]; $F_0$, beam flux through a surface normal to the beam
[$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $F^{+}$, $F^{-}$, upward and downward diffuse fluxes [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $I(\tau,\mu)$,
azimuth-integrated diffuse intensity [$\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$]; $P(\mu,\mu')$, azimuth-averaged phase function, normalised
so that $\tfrac12\int_{-1}^{1}P\,\mathrm{d}\mu' = 1$ [-]; $\gamma_1$ to $\gamma_4$, two-stream coefficients [-];
$\mu_1$, closure angle cosine [-]; $\beta_0$, $\beta_1$, $\beta$, backscattered fractions [-]; $\lambda$, eigenvalue
[-]; $\Gamma$, coupling ratio [-]; $a$, hemispheric-mean auxiliary [-]. Here $\mu$ is positive upward and $\tau$
increases downward from the top.

The default, without `planck`, is the shortwave path: Toon's quadrature row on delta-scaled inputs, the
"delta-quadrature" of Toon Table 2. With `planck` the longwave kernel uses the hemispheric-mean row and no beam.
Aliases: Coakley-Chylek models 1 and 2 (delta-function and hemispheric-constant rows), Shettle-Weinman (Eddington),
Liou (quadrature).

### Derivation

**Step 1: the exact flux equations.** For the diffuse intensity, integrated over azimuth, the transfer equation
with a collimated beam incident in direction $-\mu_0$ is Meador and Weaver's eq. (7), written with $\omega$ outside
the phase function:

$$
\mu\frac{\partial I(\tau,\mu)}{\partial\tau} = I(\tau,\mu)
  - \frac{\omega}{2}\int_{-1}^{1} P(\mu,\mu')\,I(\tau,\mu')\,\mathrm{d}\mu'
  - \frac{\omega}{2} F_0\, P(\mu,-\mu_0)\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} .
$$

Integrating it over $0 < \mu \le 1$, and over $-1 \le \mu < 0$ after replacing $\mu$ by $-\mu$, with
$F^{\pm}(\tau) = \int_0^1 \mu\, I(\tau,\pm\mu)\,\mathrm{d}\mu$ and the reciprocity
$P(\mu,-\mu_0) = P(\mu_0,-\mu)$, gives Meador and Weaver's eqs. (10) and (11) in this report's notation:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{+}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} &= \int_0^1 I(\tau,\mu)\,\mathrm{d}\mu
  - \frac{\omega}{2}\int_0^1\!\!\int_{-1}^{1} P(\mu,\mu')\,I(\tau,\mu')\,\mathrm{d}\mu'\,\mathrm{d}\mu
  - \omega F_0 \beta_0\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} , \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{-}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} &= -\int_0^1 I(\tau,-\mu)\,\mathrm{d}\mu
  + \frac{\omega}{2}\int_0^1\!\!\int_{-1}^{1} P(-\mu,\mu')\,I(\tau,\mu')\,\mathrm{d}\mu'\,\mathrm{d}\mu
  + \omega F_0 (1-\beta_0)\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-moments}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-moments check_ch02_closures.py [C1] -->

with the backscattered fraction of the beam $\beta_0 = \tfrac12\int_0^1 P(\mu_0,-\mu')\,\mathrm{d}\mu'$. Meador and
Weaver's $p$ contains $\omega$ (their eq. 2); here $\omega$ is written out. No approximation has been made yet.

**Step 2: the closure.** Each integral over $I$ in @eq-ch02-closures-moments is a linear functional of the
intensity. An assumed shape $I(\tau,\pm\mu) = a_{\pm}(\mu)F^{+} + b_{\pm}(\mu)F^{-}$ that reproduces the definition of
$F^{\pm}$ turns the system into

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{+}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} &= \gamma_1 F^{+} - \gamma_2 F^{-} - \gamma_3\,\omega F_0\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} , \\
\frac{\mathrm{d}F^{-}}{\mathrm{d}\tau} &= \gamma_2 F^{+} - \gamma_1 F^{-} + \gamma_4\,\omega F_0\, e^{-\tau/\mu_0} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-ode}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-ode check_ch02_closures.py [C21] -->

which is Toon's eqs. (11) to (14) with $F_0 = \pi F_s$. @eq-ch02-closures-ode is solved per layer in
`toon_mckay89_shortwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}});
in the thermal form, with the beam terms replaced by the Planck source of @sec-ch02-conservation, in
`toon_mckay89_longwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}}).
The same coefficient must multiply $F^{+}$ in the upward equation and $F^{-}$ in the downward one; the check confirms
this symmetry for every closure below.

**Step 3: Eddington.** The Eddington shape is $I(\tau,\pm\mu) = \tfrac12[(2\pm3\mu)F^{+} + (2\mp3\mu)F^{-}]$
(Meador-Weaver eq. 30), with $P$ truncated after its $l = 1$ Legendre term, $P(\mu,\mu') = 1 + 3g\mu\mu'$. The two
integrals of @eq-ch02-closures-moments become

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^1 I(\tau,\mu)\,\mathrm{d}\mu &= \tfrac14\left(7F^{+} + F^{-}\right) , \\
\frac12\int_0^1\!\!\int_{-1}^{1} P\,I\,\mathrm{d}\mu'\,\mathrm{d}\mu &=
  \tfrac14\left[(4+3g)F^{+} + (4-3g)F^{-}\right] ,
\end{aligned}
$$

and comparison with @eq-ch02-closures-ode gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_1 &= \tfrac14\left[7 - \omega(4+3g)\right] , \\
\gamma_2 &= -\tfrac14\left[1 - \omega(4-3g)\right] , \\
\gamma_3 &= \beta_0 = \tfrac14\left(2 - 3g\mu_0\right) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-eddington}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-eddington check_ch02_closures.py [C2] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch02-closures-eddington reference row, not evaluated by the Toon kernels -->

and $\gamma_4 = 1 - \gamma_3$, the Eddington rows of Meador-Weaver Table 1 and Toon Table 1 (check `[C1]` compares the
$\gamma_4$ integrated from @eq-ch02-closures-moments with $1 - \gamma_3$ of the printed row). Shettle and Weinman's
method is this row (Toon p. 16,290; Meador-Weaver p. 633).[^ch02-closures-papers]

**Step 4: quadrature.** The quadrature shape puts all the intensity at one angle,
$I(\tau,\pm\mu) = F^{\pm}\,\delta(\mu - \mu_1)/\mu_1$ with $\mu_1 = 3^{-1/2}$. Then
$\int_0^1 I\,\mathrm{d}\mu = F^{\pm}/\mu_1$, and the scattering integral becomes
$(\omega/\mu_1)[(1-\beta_1)F^{+} + \beta_1F^{-}]$ with $\beta_1 = \tfrac12\int_0^1 P(\mu_1,-\mu')\,\mathrm{d}\mu'$
(Meador-Weaver eqs. 34, 37, 38). Liou's rule evaluates that integral and $\beta_0$ with the same single point,
$\beta_1 = \tfrac12 P(\mu_1,-\mu_1) = \tfrac12(1 - 3g\mu_1^2) = \tfrac12(1-g)$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_1 &= \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\left[2 - \omega(1+g)\right] , \\
\gamma_2 &= \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\,\omega(1-g) , \\
\gamma_3 &= \tfrac12\left(1 - \sqrt3\, g\mu_0\right) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-quadrature}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-quadrature check_ch02_toon_coefficients.py [C4] -->

with $\gamma_4 = \tfrac12(1 + \sqrt3\, g\mu_0)$ from the same rule (Meador-Weaver eq. 42).
@eq-ch02-closures-quadrature is computed as `g1`, `g2`, `g3` and `g4` in `toon_mckay89_shortwave`
({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}}), on the delta-scaled
$\omega$ and $g$.

**Step 5: hemispheric mean.** The hemispheric-mean shape is constant in each hemisphere, $I(\tau,\pm\mu) = 2F^{\pm}$,
and the phase function is $1+g$ in the forward hemisphere and $1-g$ in the backward one (Toon Table 1, footnote). The
backscattered fraction is then $\beta = \tfrac12(1-g)$, which in Meador and Weaver's hemispheric-constant row
$\gamma_1 = 2[1 - \omega(1-\beta)]$, $\gamma_2 = 2\omega\beta$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_1 &= 2 - \omega(1+g) , \\
\gamma_2 &= \omega(1-g) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-hemispheric}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-hemispheric check_ch02_closures.py [C11] -->

@eq-ch02-closures-hemispheric is the row of `toon_mckay89_longwave`
({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}}). Toon gives no $\gamma_3$
for this row: the longwave path has no beam. The kernel does not form $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$.
It writes the eigenvalue and the coupling ratio of @sec-ch02-conservation through
$a = [(1-\omega)/(1-\omega g)]^{1/2}$. From @eq-ch02-closures-hemispheric, $\gamma_1 - \gamma_2 = 2(1-\omega)$ and
$\gamma_1 + \gamma_2 = 2(1-\omega g)$. With $u = 1 - \omega g$ this is $\gamma_1 = u(1+a^2)$ and
$\gamma_2 = u(1-a^2)$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lambda &= \left(\gamma_1^2 - \gamma_2^2\right)^{1/2} = 2a(1-\omega g) , \\
\Gamma &= \frac{\gamma_1 - \lambda}{\gamma_2} = \frac{(1-a)^2}{(1-a)(1+a)} = \frac{1-a}{1+a} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-hm-a}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-hm-a check_ch02_toon_coefficients.py [C15] -->

which `toon_mckay89_longwave` computes as `alp`, `lam` and `gam`
({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}}). The kernel's `term` is
$1/(\gamma_1+\gamma_2)$ of Toon's eq. (27), and its source-function factors `g`, `h`, `xj`, `xk` equal Toon's Table 3
$G$, $H$, $J$, $K$ once Toon's $Y_1 \pm Y_2$ are read as $\pi$ times the kernel's `xk1`, `xk2`.

**Step 6: the other named closures.** The same procedure with the true phase function kept in $\beta_0$, $\beta_1$
or $\beta$ gives the remaining Meador-Weaver rows exactly: modified Eddington, modified quadrature, hemispheric
constant (Coakley-Chylek model 2, Meador-Weaver p. 637), delta function ($\mu_1 = \mu_0$, $\beta_1 = \beta_0$;
Coakley-Chylek model 1, p. 638) and the hybrid of their eq. (58). The closures of King and Harshvardhan and of
Wiscombe and Grams are named in the outline but are not reproduced: neither is defined in a paper read for this
chapter.

**Step 7: discrete ordinates with two streams.** The discrete-ordinate equations of Stamnes et al. [@reading01]
with $N = 1$ use the double-Gauss node $\mu_1 = \tfrac12$ with weight 1. The two coupling matrices of their eq. (7b)
are then numbers, equal to $-\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$; their eigenvalue $k$ is $\lambda$, and the ratio of the
eigenvector components is $\Gamma$. The coefficients are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\gamma_1 &= 2 - \omega\left(1 + \tfrac34 g\right) , \\
\gamma_2 &= \omega\left(1 - \tfrac34 g\right) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-closures-nstr2}
<!-- equation-check: eq-ch02-closures-nstr2 check_ch02_closures.py [C20] -->
<!-- equation-source: eq-ch02-closures-nstr2 DISORT with two streams, not evaluated by the Toon kernels -->

which is Meador-Weaver eqs. (37)-(38) with $\mu_1 = \tfrac12$ and $\beta_1 = \tfrac12 - \tfrac38 g$. Each differs from
@eq-ch02-closures-hemispheric by $\omega g/4$: DISORT with two streams is not the hemispheric mean unless $g = 0$.

**What is exact.** @eq-ch02-closures-moments is exact. The closure is the only approximation, and its error is a
property of the radiation field, not a power of a step size. Every coefficient above follows from its ansatz without
further approximation, and every coefficient the Toon kernels evaluate equals its table entry identically. The check
is `derivation-checks/check_ch02_closures.py` (the closures) with `derivation-checks/check_ch02_toon_coefficients.py`
(the code).

### Numerical method

The closure has no discretisation of its own. Its coefficients are constants per layer, spectral point and column,
evaluated in closed form in the layer loop of each Toon kernel, with the round-off of a few multiplications. The
exception is $\omega = 1$, where $\lambda$ is a difference of equal numbers (@sec-ch02-conservation). The figure of this scheme is not provided: its module is not written yet.

: Code map of the two-stream closures. {#tbl-ch02-closures-code}

1. `RadiationBandOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/radiation/radiation_band.cpp RadiationBandOptionsImpl::from_yaml repo=pyharp >}})
   copies the band's `flags` for `solver: toon`; a `toon:` block may set them again.
2. `ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl::planck` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.hpp ToonMcKay89OptionsImpl::planck repo=pyharp >}})
   is true when `flags` contains `planck`.
3. `ToonMcKay89Impl::forward` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89.cpp ToonMcKay89Impl::forward repo=pyharp >}}) picks
   the kernel; the longwave path requires level temperatures.
4. `toon_mckay89_shortwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_shortwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_shortwave repo=pyharp >}})
   forms @eq-ch02-closures-quadrature per layer; `g2` exactly 0 becomes `1e-10`.
5. `toon_mckay89_longwave` ({{< code src/rtsolver/toon_mckay89_longwave_impl.h toon_mckay89_longwave repo=pyharp >}})
   forms @eq-ch02-closures-hm-a per layer.

All 22 claims of the closure check and all 25 of the code check pass.[^ch02-closures-run] The checks are symbolic and
device independent. The pyharp test was read at the pin, not run; no pyharp test asserts a two-stream coefficient
(`DeviceTest.simple_toon_mckay89` runs both paths but asserts nothing).

### Limits

- The two-stream approximation error is not bounded in this section; the solver-comparison chapter measures it.
- King-Harshvardhan and Wiscombe-Grams closures: not provided, because their papers were not read for this chapter.
- The longwave path has no beam: `toon_mckay89_longwave` takes no beam input, so a nonzero `fbeam` on a `planck`
  band has no effect (from reading `ToonMcKay89Impl::forward`, not run).
- A two-stream DISORT run (@eq-ch02-closures-nstr2) is not a substitute for the hemispheric mean.
